CHIEF COMPLAINT
Abnormal lab finding - positive Lyme titer.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Michelle is a 31-year-old female presenting with a positive Lyme titer. Patient reports an insect bite sustained while hiking in the woods a couple of weeks ago. She describes feeling tired with lack of energy. She has swollen joints in her elbows that are painful. She endorses body aches, nausea, and decreased appetite, able to tolerate only toast and crackers. She notes a bull's-eye rash on her abdomen. She denies high fevers. Regarding her diabetes, she reports blood sugars have been okay with occasional highs and lows but nothing out of range.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses nausea, joint pain, and body aches. She denies abdominal pain, diarrhea, and fever.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Hypertension

MEDICATIONS
Metformin for diabetes
Lisinopril 10 milligrams daily for hypertension

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports hiking in the woods a couple of weeks ago, which is believed to be where she acquired the insect bite. She has been monitoring blood pressure at home and avoiding salty foods.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: No fever at this time. Cardiovascular and respiratory exam normal. Extremities: Bilateral elbow joint swelling with pain to palpation. Skin: Bull's-eye rash on left side of abdomen, warm to palpation, non-tender, no evidence of cellulitis. Remainder of exam normal.

RESULTS
Lyme titer: Elevated
Complete metabolic panel and white blood cell count: Normal, no elevation

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Newly diagnosed Lyme disease: Start doxycycline 100 milligrams twice daily for three weeks. Consult with infectious disease doctor. Follow-up appointment next week.
2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c to assess need for changes to metformin dosing. Continue current metformin therapy.
3. Hypertension: Currently well-controlled. Continue lisinopril 10 milligrams daily. Order lipid panel. Patient to continue monitoring blood pressure at home regularly. Refill lisinopril prescribed.
